title: Build a learning curve, and score a choice honestly
brief: Build a learning curve and read it, simulate why the best of many noisy scores is too good, and use nested cross-validation to score a penalty choice on data it never saw.
hints: validation_split: order = np.random.default_rng(seed).permutation(n); the first int(round(val_fraction * n)) entries are the validation rows and the rest are the pool.

learning_curve calls validation_split once, then for each size trains on pool[:size], so every training set contains the one before it. Score the training error on pool[:size] and the validation error on val_idx.

diagnose_curve looks only at the last entry of each curve: gap = val[-1] - train[-1]. A gap above gap_threshold is 'overfit'; otherwise a validation error above high_threshold is 'underfit'; otherwise 'good'.
best_of_m_gap: estimates = true_error + noise_sd * rng.standard_normal((trials, m)). The winner of each trial is estimates.min(axis=1); return the mean of true_error minus that minimum.

empirical_rademacher: signs = rng.choice(np.array([-1.0, 1.0]), size=(num_draws, n)). Then losses_matrix @ signs.T has shape (num_models, num_draws). Take .max(axis=0), then the mean, then divide by n.

nested_cv_score: for each outer test fold, pick the penalty with the lowest mean cross_val_score on the outer training rows only, refit on all outer training rows, and score the outer test fold. Return the mean of the outer fold errors.
